newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain adjourns trial of alleged Qatari spies.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain adjourns trial of alleged Qatari spies.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court has adjourned a trial of two Qataris charged with spying, a lawyer and a government official said on Thursday.
"The court has adjourned the trial of the Qataris to December 14 at the request of their defence lawyers," a lawyer told Reuters. A government official confirmed the postponement.
The trial of the two Qataris -- a man and a woman -- began on Wednesday on charges of gathering intelligence for the Qatari government and accepting money from Doha to undermine Bahrain's security.

The defendants, Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri, had confessed before an investigating judge to spying for Qatar, a crime for which the penalty is either execution or a long prison term.
Qatar has denied they were spies.
Bahraini newspapers said on Thursday al-Baker wept and told his relatives outside the court "the Qatari intelligence service had given him no choice".
The spy charges have raised tensions between Bahrain and Qatar, already at loggerheads over small but potentially rich Gulf islands controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Bahrain has said it would boycott a Gulf Arab summit to be held in Doha on Saturday.
